title: ADR-001: Auth Library Selection
content:
ADR-001: Authentication Library Selection

Status

Accepted — Superseded by none.

Context

We needed to choose an authentication library for the Auth Service. The requirements were:

  • Support for JWT with RS256 signing
  • Built-in refresh token rotation
  • Go-native implementation (no CGO dependencies)
  • Active maintenance with security audit history

We evaluated three options:

  1. golang-jwt/jwt — most popular, minimal dependencies
  2. lestrrat-go/jwx — full JWK/JWKS support, more complex
  3. cristalhq/jwt — zero allocation design, minimal API

Decision

We chose golang-jwt/jwt v5 for its balance of simplicity, widespread adoption, and security track record.

The JWK support from lestrrat-go/jwx is not needed at this stage since we control both issuers and consumers. If we introduce external identity providers (e.g., Cognito, Auth0), we will revisit this decision.

Consequences

Positive:

  • Simple API reduces chance of implementation errors
  • Extensive community usage means faster bug detection
  • Easy to find examples and audit existing integrations

Negative:

  • Limited JWK/JWKS support may require a library change if we add external IdPs
  • No built-in key rotation utilities — we implement our own

Alternatives Considered

Library Reason Not Chosen
lestrrat-go/jwx Over-engineered for our current needs; complex API
cristalhq/jwt Too minimal; lacks community validation
dgrijalva/jwt-go Deprecated, known CVEs
